title: Acts — Predicate Selection Is the Fact, Not the Operation
note: The precedence rule here keys on HOW THE TARGET SET WAS CHOSEN, not on what the operation does. An update to one identified record and an update to every record matching a filter are the same verb; what differs is that the second act's blast radius is not fixed by the act itself — nobody, including the sender, knows how many rows move until it runs. That is the fact a verifier needs, so the bulk label wins whenever selection is predicate-based. The same rule governs creation and deletion, which is why the bulk labels are a family rather than one special case.
